main_text.l: coronam justitiæ, quam reponit Dominus omnibus ijs, qui ita vitam instituunt, ut adventum ejus illustrem exoptent ac diligant.

Tradamus nos in disciplinam Christo, qui est sapientia Patris, ejus hæc schola est, hic sapientiam docet parvulos: is invitat suos ad hoc exercitium, dicens per Prophetam, beatos illos esse, qui ferunt semen verbi divini, super omnem locum aquosum, super cœtum videlicet & multitudinem populorum; quique pedem bouis triturantis segetem Domini, & asini Christum gestantes, in agrum Ecclesiæ immittunt, ut labore eorum subactus, fructum uberrimum Domino proferat. Cedet ipsis proventus justitiæ præciosissimus, longe alius ab illorum messe, qui in carnis & corporis fundo colendo occupati, ex carne corruptionem metunt: nam qui semen Spiritus, pio sanctoque animo, spirituali Dei agro committit, ipse ex spiritu vitam æternam metet: cujus primitias hic degustabit, & cum Davide Deo confitebitur, Quam multum Domine est bonum tuum, quod sepofuisti [?] timentibus te; quod operatus es, sperantibus in te, eorum filijs hominum. Verum quidem est, quod & ibi corripiet nos ac tentabit pa-terna

page.notes: Left margin note "Ut in hoc mundo, vita beatissima fruantur." is printed in three lines and italic, with the words split across lines as "Vt in hoc / mundo. vita / beatissima / fruantur."; transcribed as one note. Word "sepofuisti" is doubtful (possibly "suscepisti" with ligature); marked [?]. The final word "paterna" is split across the last line as "pa-" and "terna"; kept as printed. The Gal. 6. 8. marginal reference is beside the line "qui semen Spiritus". Long s rendered as s throughout; "&" retained as printed in "&" and ligature "ct" in "subactus" normalised. Print shows "Vt" which was changed to "Ut" per the u/v rule.
